correctness.rationale: Every red edge uv has red-degrees r(u)+r(v)=5; blue edges have sum3, because exactly three of six neighbouring edges are red. This forces the degree-type path 0–3–2–1–4 and 5 distance layers, each vertex with i predecessors and 4−i successors. Connectedness ensures all classes; converse colours consecutive layers alternately. Layer edge double-counting gives sizes (a,4a,6a,4a,a), hence 16a vertices and bipartiteness. Independent breadth-first layer tests found 16/8 centers in Q4 and switched Q4, respectively, with 24/22 four-cycles. This is full proof, finite examples only check sharpness.

value.rationale: Natural exact structural classification translating a local edge-colour condition into completely regular code geometry for all connected quartic graphs, with sharp divisibility, bipartiteness, and different counts on smallest nonisomorphic witnesses. Independent of the already known Q4-only special case.

final_claim: For every finite connected simple 4-regular graph, named two-colour strong-majority edge assignments are in bijection with completely regular radius-four codes of intersection array (4,3,2,1;1,2,3,4). All such graphs are bipartite, have order divisible by16, and Q4 and a switched cube have respectively 16 and 8 named colourings.
limitations: Prior Q4 special case known and not counted as novelty.
Broader coding-theory literature could implicitly imply a related all-graph layer criterion; best-of-knowledge originality only.
